sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
**Project 13:** CUSTOMER SEGMENTATION (UNSUPERVISED LEARNING)

**What you'll learn:**
- KMeans Clustering
- DBSCAN Clustering
- Elbow Method (finding optimal K)
- Silhouette Score & Analysis
- Cluster visualization & interpretation
- When to use KMeans vs DBSCAN
- PCA for visualization of high-dimensional clusters

**Dataset:** Synthetic customer data (sklearn make_blobs)
- Customer spending patterns
- No target variable (unsupervised!)

**Type:** UNSUPERVISED LEARNING (Clustering Deep Dive)

sections.title: Step 1: Create Customer Data
sections.body:
```python
unsupervised_intro = """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                   UNSUPERVISED LEARNING                              ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                      ║
║  SUPERVISED: We have labels (target variable)                        ║
║    → Classification, Regression                                      ║
║    → "Given features, predict the target"                            ║
║                                                                      ║
║  UNSUPERVISED: NO labels! Find hidden patterns                       ║
║    → Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction                            ║
║    → "Group similar data points together"                            ║
║                                                                      ║
║  USE CASES:                                                          ║
║  • Customer segmentation (group similar customers)                   ║
║  • Anomaly detection (find unusual data points)                      ║
║  • Market basket analysis                                            ║
║  • Image compression                                                 ║
║  • Feature extraction                                                ║
║                                                                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
"""
print(unsupervised_intro)

# Generate realistic customer data with known clusters
np.random.seed(42)

# Create 5 customer segments
n_customers = 1000

# Segment data: [annual_income, spending_score, age, visits_per_month, avg_purchase]
segments = {
    "Budget Shoppers": {"center": [30, 20, 45, 2, 15], "n": 250},
    "Average Customers": {"center": [50, 50, 35, 5, 40], "n": 300},
    "High Earners Low Spend": {"center": [80, 25, 50, 3, 30], "n": 150},
    "Target Customers": {"center": [70, 80, 30, 10, 70], "n": 200},
    "Premium Customers": {"center": [90, 90, 40, 15, 100], "n": 100},
}

data_list = []
for seg_name, seg_info in segments.items():
    center = seg_info["center"]
    n = seg_info["n"]
    data = np.random.randn(n, 5) * [10, 15, 8, 2, 12] + center
    for row in data:
        data_list.append(row)

df = pd.DataFrame(
    data_list,
    columns=[
        "annual_income",
        "spending_score",
        "age",
        "visits_per_month",
        "avg_purchase",
    ],
)

# Clip to realistic ranges
df["annual_income"] = df["annual_income"].clip(10, 120)
df["spending_score"] = df["spending_score"].clip(1, 100)
df["age"] = df["age"].clip(18, 70).astype(int)
df["visits_per_month"] = df["visits_per_month"].clip(0, 30).round(1)
df["avg_purchase"] = df["avg_purchase"].clip(5, 150).round(2)

print(f"Shape: {df.shape}")
print(f"\nHead:\n{df.head()}")
print(f"\nDescribe:\n{df.describe()}")
```

sections.title: Step 4: Kmeans Clustering
sections.body:
```python
kmeans_explanation = """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                      KMEANS CLUSTERING                               ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                      ║
║  HOW IT WORKS:                                                       ║
║  1. Choose K (number of clusters)                                    ║
║  2. Randomly place K centroids                                       ║
║  3. Assign each point to nearest centroid                            ║
║  4. Move centroids to mean of assigned points                        ║
║  5. Repeat steps 3-4 until convergence                               ║
║                                                                      ║
║  PROS:                                                               ║
║  ✓ Simple and fast                                                   ║
║  ✓ Works well with spherical clusters                                ║
║  ✓ Scales to large datasets                                          ║
║                                                                      ║
║  CONS:                                                               ║
║  ✗ Must specify K in advance                                         ║
║  ✗ Sensitive to initialization (use n_init=10)                       ║
║  ✗ Assumes spherical clusters (bad for irregular shapes)             ║
║  ✗ Sensitive to outliers                                             ║
║                                                                      ║
║  FINDING OPTIMAL K:                                                  ║
║  1. Elbow Method: Plot inertia vs K, look for "elbow"                ║
║  2. Silhouette Score: Higher = better defined clusters               ║
║                                                                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
"""
print(kmeans_explanation)

# --- ELBOW METHOD ---
print("Finding optimal K with Elbow Method...")
inertias = []
silhouettes = []
K_range = range(2, 11)

for k in K_range:
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)
    inertias.append(kmeans.inertia_)
    silhouettes.append(silhouette_score(X_scaled, labels))
    print(f"  K={k}: Inertia={kmeans.inertia_:.0f}, Silhouette={silhouettes[-1]:.4f}")

# Plot Elbow & Silhouette
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

axes[0].plot(K_range, inertias, "bo-", linewidth=2, markersize=8)
axes[0].set_xlabel("Number of Clusters (K)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Inertia (Within-Cluster Sum of Squares)")
axes[0].set_title("Elbow Method")
axes[0].axvline(x=5, color="red", linestyle="--", label="Optimal K=5")
axes[0].legend()

axes[1].plot(K_range, silhouettes, "ro-", linewidth=2, markersize=8)
axes[1].set_xlabel("Number of Clusters (K)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("Silhouette Score")
axes[1].set_title("Silhouette Score (higher = better)")
axes[1].axvline(x=5, color="red", linestyle="--", label="Optimal K=5")
axes[1].legend()

plt.suptitle("Finding Optimal K", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("project_13_optimal_k.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()

# --- Apply KMeans with optimal K ---
optimal_k = 5
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=optimal_k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
df["kmeans_cluster"] = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)

print(f"\nKMeans with K={optimal_k}:")
print(f"  Silhouette Score: {silhouette_score(X_scaled, df['kmeans_cluster']):.4f}")
print(f"  Cluster sizes: {df['kmeans_cluster'].value_counts().sort_index().to_dict()}")
```

sections.title: Step 5: Dbscan Clustering
sections.body:
```python
dbscan_explanation = """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                      DBSCAN CLUSTERING                               ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                      ║
║  HOW IT WORKS:                                                       ║
║  1. For each point, find all neighbors within eps distance           ║
║  2. If ≥ min_samples neighbors → it's a CORE point                  ║
║  3. Core points connected by density → same cluster                  ║
║  4. Non-core points near core points → BORDER points                 ║
║  5. Points not near any core point → NOISE (-1)                      ║
║                                                                      ║
║  PROS:                                                               ║
║  ✓ No need to specify K!                                             ║
║  ✓ Finds clusters of ANY shape                                       ║
║  ✓ Automatically detects outliers (noise)                            ║
║                                                                      ║
║  CONS:                                                               ║
║  ✗ Need to tune eps and min_samples                                  ║
║  ✗ Struggles with varying density clusters                           ║
║  ✗ Doesn't work well in high dimensions                              ║
║                                                                      ║
║  PARAMETERS:                                                         ║
║  - eps: Maximum distance between neighbors (try 0.3 - 1.5)          ║
║  - min_samples: Minimum points to form cluster (try 5 - 20)         ║
║                                                                      ║
║  WHEN TO USE:                                                        ║
║  KMeans → spherical clusters, know K                                 ║
║  DBSCAN → irregular shapes, outlier detection, unknown K             ║
║                                                                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
"""
print(dbscan_explanation)

# Try different eps values
print("Trying different eps values...")
for eps in [0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5]:
    dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=5)
    labels = dbscan.fit_predict(X_scaled)
    n_clusters = len(set(labels)) - (1 if -1 in labels else 0)
    n_noise = list(labels).count(-1)
    if n_clusters > 1:
        sil = silhouette_score(X_scaled[labels != -1], labels[labels != -1])
    else:
        sil = -1
    print(
        f"  eps={eps}: {n_clusters} clusters, {n_noise} noise points, silhouette={sil:.4f}"
    )

# Use best eps
dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=0.7, min_samples=5)
df["dbscan_cluster"] = dbscan.fit_predict(X_scaled)
print(
    f"\nDBSCAN: {df['dbscan_cluster'].nunique()} unique labels (including -1 for noise)"
)
print(f"  Cluster sizes: {df['dbscan_cluster'].value_counts().sort_index().to_dict()}")
```

sections.title: Step 6: Visualize Clusters (using Pca for 2D)
sections.body:

```python
# Reduce to 2D for visualization
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)
print(f"\nPCA explained variance: {pca.explained_variance_ratio_}")
print(f"Total explained: {pca.explained_variance_ratio_.sum():.1%}")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))

# KMeans clusters
scatter1 = axes[0].scatter(
    X_pca[:, 0], X_pca[:, 1], c=df["kmeans_cluster"], cmap="Set1", alpha=0.5, s=15
)
# Plot centroids
centers_pca = pca.transform(kmeans.cluster_centers_)
axes[0].scatter(
    centers_pca[:, 0],
    centers_pca[:, 1],
    c="black",
    marker="X",
    s=200,
    edgecolors="white",
    linewidths=2,
)
axes[0].set_title(f"KMeans (K={optimal_k})")
axes[0].legend(*scatter1.legend_elements(), title="Cluster", loc="best", fontsize=8)

# DBSCAN clusters
scatter2 = axes[1].scatter(
    X_pca[:, 0], X_pca[:, 1], c=df["dbscan_cluster"], cmap="Set1", alpha=0.5, s=15
)
axes[1].set_title("DBSCAN")
axes[1].legend(*scatter2.legend_elements(), title="Cluster", loc="best", fontsize=8)

# Key feature comparison
for cluster in range(optimal_k):
    mask = df["kmeans_cluster"] == cluster
    axes[2].scatter(
        df.loc[mask, "annual_income"],
        df.loc[mask, "spending_score"],
        label=f"Cluster {cluster}",
        alpha=0.5,
        s=15,
    )
axes[2].set_xlabel("Annual Income")
axes[2].set_ylabel("Spending Score")
axes[2].set_title("KMeans: Income vs Spending")
axes[2].legend(fontsize=8)

plt.suptitle("Cluster Visualization", fontsize=16, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("project_13_clusters.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Step 7: Interpret Clusters (The Most Important Step!)
sections.body:
```python
print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("CLUSTER INTERPRETATION (Business Insights!)")
print("=" * 60)

cluster_summary = (
    df.groupby("kmeans_cluster")[
        ["annual_income", "spending_score", "age", "visits_per_month", "avg_purchase"]
    ]
    .mean()
    .round(1)
)

print(f"\nCluster Profiles (means):")
print(cluster_summary)

# Interpret each cluster
print("\nCluster Interpretations:")
for cluster in range(optimal_k):
    profile = cluster_summary.loc[cluster]
    n = (df["kmeans_cluster"] == cluster).sum()
    print(f"\n  Cluster {cluster} ({n} customers):")
    print(
        f"    Income: ${profile['annual_income']:.0f}K | "
        f"Spending: {profile['spending_score']:.0f}/100 | "
        f"Age: {profile['age']:.0f} | "
        f"Visits/mo: {profile['visits_per_month']:.1f} | "
        f"Avg Purchase: ${profile['avg_purchase']:.0f}"
    )

# Visualization of cluster profiles
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(12, 6))

# Normalize for radar-like comparison
cluster_norm = (cluster_summary - cluster_summary.min()) / (
    cluster_summary.max() - cluster_summary.min()
)
cluster_norm.plot(kind="bar", ax=ax, width=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("Cluster")
ax.set_ylabel("Normalized Value")
ax.set_title("Cluster Profiles Comparison")
ax.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc="upper left")
ax.set_xticklabels([f"Cluster {i}" for i in range(optimal_k)], rotation=0)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("project_13_profiles.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Step 8: Silhouette Analysis (Quality Check)
sections.body:
```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(10, 6))

sample_silhouettes = silhouette_samples(X_scaled, df["kmeans_cluster"])
y_lower = 10

for i in range(optimal_k):
    cluster_sil = sample_silhouettes[df["kmeans_cluster"] == i]
    cluster_sil.sort()

    y_upper = y_lower + len(cluster_sil)
    color = plt.colormaps["Set1"](i / optimal_k)
    ax.fill_betweenx(
        np.arange(y_lower, y_upper), 0, cluster_sil, facecolor=color, alpha=0.7
    )
    ax.text(-0.05, y_lower + 0.5 * len(cluster_sil), str(i), fontsize=12)
    y_lower = y_upper + 10

avg_sil = silhouette_score(X_scaled, df["kmeans_cluster"])
ax.axvline(x=avg_sil, color="red", linestyle="--", label=f"Avg: {avg_sil:.3f}")
ax.set_xlabel("Silhouette Coefficient")
ax.set_ylabel("Cluster")
ax.set_title("Silhouette Analysis")
ax.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("project_13_silhouette.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()

print(
    """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  KEY TAKEAWAYS - UNSUPERVISED LEARNING                              ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                      ║
║  SCALING IS MANDATORY for clustering!                                ║
║                                                                      ║
║  KMEANS:                                                             ║
║  • Must specify K → use Elbow + Silhouette to find it                ║
║  • Good for spherical, equal-size clusters                           ║
║  • Fast and scalable                                                 ║
║                                                                      ║
║  DBSCAN:                                                             ║
║  • No need for K → finds clusters automatically                      ║
║  • Finds any shape + detects outliers                                ║
║  • Need to tune eps and min_samples                                  ║
║                                                                      ║
║  EVALUATION:                                                         ║
║  • Silhouette Score: -1 to 1 (higher = better)                       ║
║    > 0.7: Excellent   > 0.5: Good   > 0.25: Fair                    ║
║  • Elbow Method: Look for the "bend" in the curve                    ║
║  • Business interpretation: most important evaluation!               ║
║                                                                      ║
║  PCA: Reduces dimensions for visualization (2D/3D)                   ║
║                                                                      ║
║  WORKFLOW:                                                           ║
║  Scale → Find K → Cluster → Evaluate → Interpret                    ║
║                                                                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
"""
)
```
